title: Moving to Chicago and choosing the trombone
summary: The family moved to Chicago about 1920; he wanted trumpet, but his cousin took it, so he got a mail-order trombone and rode the L to lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: When did you first take up music then?
I taken up music after I moved to Chicago. Yeah, that, we moved to Chicago possibly, it was in 19 or 20. I'm not, I'm not sure. It's very vague because I was still very young at that time.
About 1920 I would say. We'd be, be right.
Who did you study with or did you pick up the trombone yourself? Was that your first instrument?

No, I didn't pick up the trombone myself. In fact, my first love was the trumpet. I wanted, wanted a trumpet. But my family is very small. There's only about four of us in our immediate family. And my cousin is four years older than I am. So they wanted to start us to take in music at the same time. So he picked the trumpet. So it had to fall to me for the second choice. So my second choice was the trombone. I picked the trombone. And I, you know, stuck right with it. And my mother, it was quite a hardship on her to give me lessons and whatnot. I never will forget my first instrument. It was bought from Sears and Roebuck. Out of a catalog. I think it cost something like 1675. It was a beautiful instrument. A gautier. A gautier or something that had a French name. It was nickel plated. I couldn't afford the case or anything. So as I would go to take my music lesson, I'd have to get on the L. Because my lesson, I'd take my lessons on the south side from W.L. Jackson. He had a music school over here. And I would get on the L with the trombone all out, no case or nothing. People would be looking, but I didn't mind.
